mu_name_from: MuMain loads helm indexes 10 to 14 from HelmElf{i+1} rather than HelmMale (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 148: `AccessModel(MODEL_HELM + i + 10, ..., L"HelmElf", i + 1)`), so index 10 is HelmElf01, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Vine Helm. mu.db agrees: code 3594, group 7 index 10, Player/HelmElf01.bmd.
why_this_one: The Fairy Elf's own first set, and the one set of the three that nobody sells: no shelf in Lorencia carries Vine, so this is a drop and a thing to look at. It is here because the Armour select had a single glove under her name and a set of one piece is a set you cannot see.
profile_from: Not armour, whose default is plate_steel: nothing in this set is a forged plate. See profiles/soft_armour.json, which exists for these three sets.
keeps_head_from:
ZzzCharacter.cpp, SetCharacterScale. The client keeps a BODYPART_HEAD beside BODYPART_HELM and normally sets it to -1 - a helm replaces the head. For a short list of helms it sets it to `MODEL_BODY_HELM + c->SkinIndex` instead, which is HelmClass{SkinIndex+1}.bmd, the bare head of the character's own class, and draws it under the helm:

    if (Helm == MODEL_HELM || Helm == MODEL_PAD_HELM || Helm == MODEL_HELM + 63 ||
        Helm == MODEL_HELM + 68 || Helm == MODEL_HELM + 65 || Helm == MODEL_HELM + 70 ||
        (Helm >= MODEL_VINE_HELM && Helm <= MODEL_SPIRIT_HELM))
        c->BodyPart[BODYPART_HEAD].Type = MODEL_BODY_HELM + c->SkinIndex;
    else
        c->BodyPart[BODYPART_HEAD].Type = -1;

In 0.75's numbering that is helm 0 (Bronze), 2 (Pad) and 10 to 13 (Vine, Silk, Wind, Spirit); the four in the sixties are later seasons. The rule is about the mesh rather than about the item: these are the open helms - a circlet, a coif, a band - and they carry no face of their own, where the Leather Helm carries 27 triangles of skin_barbarian_01 inside its own model and needs no head under it. Helm 10 is MODEL_VINE_HELM, the first of the range MODEL_VINE_HELM to MODEL_SPIRIT_HELM.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateArmor(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)`, so slot 2 is group 7, 3 is 8 and 4 is 9.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 0, 1 - the Fairy Elf alone. Sixty agility beside thirty strength is the row saying the same thing in stats.

sheet_from: Data/Player/head_a01.OZJ (64x32), from MuMain, and it is the only sheet the model names - one mesh, 58 triangles, no hide and no skin. The .bmd names head_a01.jpg.
sheet_note: head_a01 is a circlet rather than a helm: a band of dark hide with a raised scroll of vine worked along it, drawn twice across a 64x32 strip. Mean (81, 55, 37) at chroma 44, the warmest brown in the three sets.
material_note: Five islands and one sheet: head_a01's 58 triangles, the vine circlet, split by the weld into a band, two ends and two slivers. leather throughout, the profile's default. The scrollwork is the hide raised and lit in the same brown rather than a metal inlaid into it, which is the same reading the Vine Gloves record and the thing that separates this set from the Pad set's gilt.
